purpose.is: The page service is the owner's one surface per tier: it serves the owner's page, feeds it frames from the push stream, shows its own staleness, takes the owner's answers and messages into the store, and holds the key. Everything the owner sees is on it; nothing exists outside the panel.
purpose.is-not: It is not a store (it keeps no JSONL), not a consumer (the watcher is), not a scheduler, and never typed into by a seat.
purpose.why: The page is the one durable success of four lives of bearings (L08 section 4): 142 owner messages and 42 answers in four days, median reply 32 s. What failed around it: one agent reader, agent-only producers, idle shutdown of the owner's monitor, a board that lied for six hours with nothing saying so, hand edits live without a PR, and a server that ran inside herdr and died with it. The rebuild keeps the page and replaces everything around it with supervised code that reports on itself.
purpose.decisions: D20 bearings is the one surface with the rail folded in (C51), D21 push (C52), D12 system lane (C40), D08 own supervised unit (C46), D22 display stays on the WSL host (C38), D04 state outside the repo with cleanup (C35), factorio-map-replaces-board, the look rule (brief addendum 04:45Z), bearings-stable-is-the-only-always-on-monitor, screenshot-every-page-change.

input.text: The page service subscribes once per tier (class page, filter tier=<tier> plus the global kinds health and watcher.alive) and fans the frames out to every browser tab through the SSE adapter (N-31 step 6). The tier unit start is the traversal's beginning; the subscribe is its first act.

output.text: page.state is an upsert keyed page:<page> written every second (compare-and-swap); it is how the Controls screen (N-42) and the promotion node (N-48) see the page, and how the page shows itself: the strip's MONITORING cell draws from the same record the page wrote, so a frozen page shows stale to anyone else even when its own tab looks fine.
output.leaves: The owner's answer leaves as owner.answer to N-29 (re-entry); the owner's message leaves as owner.message to N-30 (re-entry); an attachment leaves as file.stored 100 with its path under the tier's state directory.

record.field: stop (SIGTERM, 100) or crash (500, written by N-06 when the unit exits unclean)
a second instance for a tier whose port is held; exit 3

mechanism.where: Go binary coq-bearings in the control plane module (D01), run as the systemd user unit instance coq-bearings@<page>.service on the WSL host (D22), listening on 127.0.0.1 only (config listen_host), one process per tier. It serves the owner's vendored assets from the checkout the tier runs from (tools/bearings/assets/page.html, theme.css, and the map bundle for /board) re-read per request as today, so a markup-only change needs no restart.
mechanism.step: Start: load tools/bearings/config/bearings.json (validated by its schema; ${HOME}, ${project}, ${tier}, ${ticket}, ${ENV:NAME} interpolation; an unknown variable is exit 3 naming it); resolve the tier and page; refuse a second instance if the port or the page lock ${COQ_STATE}/bearings/<page>/server.json names a live pid (page.refused 409, exit 3); mint or read the 128-bit key into server.json (mode 0600; the key is never in a record, never in a log, never in a push); listen; write page.up 100.

Subscribe to N-31 as class page with since_seq 0 (a snapshot on every start: open cards, last messages_window messages with acks, rail rows, health, lamps) and keep the in-memory state the SSE adapter serves from. Reconnect by the N-31 client rule on any break.

Auth: GET /?key=<key> sets the HttpOnly cookie and redirects to /; every other route requires the cookie; the Host header must be in allowed_hosts (loopback names and the tailnet names, PR 186); 403 otherwise; body caps from config; no CORS.

Render: GET / serves page.html with the theme inlined (@@THEME@@) and a build stamp; the page opens EventSource /events and applies frames by (kind, key, version) (shared/state-store.xml#apply). The 2 s /state poll is removed; /state stays as the snapshot endpoint the page calls once on load and on a resync.

Answers: POST /answer {card, pick, words} becomes owner.answer with id minted by the page (a-...), tier, source page; the service calls Intake.Answer (N-29) and returns the ruling or the refusal; the browser keeps the answer in localStorage with state queued until a reply comes, retries 3 times (1, 2, 4 s) on a network error, then shows "not recorded" with a retry button; the watcher's stream path delivers whatever the store already holds. Messages: POST /message {id, text, files, reply_to} the same way through Inbox.Message (N-30), and the ack ladder draws from pushed ack records.

Attachments: POST /file stores under ${COQ_STATE}/bearings/<page>/files/ with the id f-..., caps file_max_bytes, inline only for the four image types, and writes file.stored 100 with the path; GET /files/<id> serves it behind the cookie.

Staleness: every second, compute state from the last frame time and write page.state; the strip's MONITORING cell shows LIVE, STALE Ns or DISCONNECTED from the pushed page.state, and every panel on the page carries the seq it was drawn from behind a fold. A page that cannot reach the store still serves itself and says so (L08 finding 5: the owner found the lie; now the page says it first).
Health: GET /health returns the page.state body plus pid and port for the watcher's probe and for N-48.
Stop: SIGTERM drains connections up to 5 s (stop_tries 3 of stop_try_ms 5000 carried as one bound), writes page.down 100, removes nothing (the key stays for the next start), exits 0.
mechanism.text: Why Go and not server.mjs: one language and one module for every supervised unit (D01, D09), a gRPC client without adding a Node dependency to a dependency-free tool, and one test harness with the fake clock. What carries forward unchanged: page.html and theme.css (the owner's), the key and cookie model, the tier config and its schema, the body caps, the Playwright suite in Podman (tests drive the Go binary the same way), and the Makefile verbs as thin wrappers over systemctl and the CLI.

Why the page service calls Intake and Inbox itself and does not only write to the store for the watcher: the owner must see his act acknowledged in the same tap; the watcher is the second path that proves it and catches a failed first call.

tiers.tier: the owner's page; never stopped on a halt; upgraded in place by a restart
the reviewer reads it; the owner confirms here a change to the owner-locked assets (nodes/N-48/spec.xml#owner-confirm)
tiers.upgrade: Stable upgrade is the one swap mechanism of nodes/N-48/spec.xml#mechanism step 3: N-48 renames the tier's current workspace pointer to the merge sha and runs systemctl --user restart coq-bearings@coq-stable: a 2 s gap in which browsers show DISCONNECTED and reconnect by themselves with Last-Event-ID; the watcher (N-27) keeps running as its own unit and the front door (N-34) restarts with the page by BindsTo, so nothing the owner typed is lost and the watch never stops; a failed probe renames the pointer back and restarts again (N-48 rollback). This closes the defect recorded at the 03:51Z checkpoint (make upgrade stopped stable and its waits; the server was replaced by hand).
tiers.key: The key is minted once per page and survives restarts in server.json; rotate-key is a CLI verb that writes a new key and a key.rotated 100 record without the key in it.

unit.name: coq-bearings@.service
unit.line: [Unit] Description=coq bearings page %i; Wants=coq.service; After=coq.service network-online.target; StartLimitIntervalSec=0

[Service] Type=simple; ExecStart=%h/.local/state/coq/coq-jev-herdr-plugin/tiers/%i/current/bin/coq-bearings serve --page %i (the binary and assets of the tier's current workspace, built by N-48 at provision); Restart=always; RestartSec=2; RestartPreventExitStatus=3; MemoryMax=256M; Environment=COQ_STATE=%h/.local/state/coq/coq-jev-herdr-plugin

start.text: Stable is enabled once with linger; dev and uat instances are started and stopped by N-48 with the ticket in the page name; a seat never runs serve by hand, and the Makefile's serve verb calls systemctl so an agent that types it still gets a unit, never a process under itself (tools/bearings/AGENTS.md NEVER example 1, kept).

wait.fallback: retry the bind 3 times 2 s apart (a lingering socket from the previous instance), then exit 4 with page.bind.failed 500; systemd restarts after RestartSec
serve the page with state DISCONNECTED and an empty deck labelled as such; retry the subscribe by the N-31 client rule; the page says what it does not know
reply 503 to the browser, which queues and retries 3 times; the watcher's stream path is the backstop; count page_intake_failed
400 to the browser with the reason; no partial file is kept (write to a temp name then rename)
close the tab's stream; EventSource reconnects
forced exit; browsers reconnect to the next instance
retry the step 3 times 5 s apart; then restore the legacy server and write cutover.failed 500

waits.no-cog: The cog that could stall this node is the service behind it being down. Timeout: 5 s per call. Fallback: the page serves itself from memory, labels everything STALE or DISCONNECTED with the age, queues the owner's acts in the browser, and the watcher plus systemd bring the path back. The owner's monitor is never silent and never dies quietly.

retries.rule: Every store-facing call retries 3 times with backoff then reports with a record and a visible state on the page; systemd is the process-level retry; the browser is the owner-act retry; nothing is dropped silently.

many-agents-at-once.readers: Any number of seats read this volume. The page assets are the owner's: one in-flight ticket may touch page.html or theme.css at a time, and every change goes dev, uat with a screenshot and card, stable (N-48).
many-agents-at-once.workers: Build tickets touch cmd/coq-bearings, internal/owner/page, tools/bearings/units/coq-bearings@.service, tools/bearings/assets (by the look ticket only), tools/bearings/config, tools/bearings/tests; the SSE adapter file belongs to N-31's ticket; the rail panel markup to N-33's.

look.rule: Every view the owner sees on this page carries the Krastorio 2 and Factorio GUI look (brief addendum 2026-10-14 ~04:45Z: "All views shown to me better have that krastorio look to it"), from the art inventory section 4 values only, in original art: outer frame #313031 with edge #4D4643 and inner ring #231C19 as a 9-slice drawn in CSS and SVG; deep inset #242324 for the message thread; shallow inset #403F40 for bubbles and the rail; caption text #FFE6C0 at heading-1 18 px bold and heading-2 15 px bold; body text #FFFFFF at 14 px; orange accent #FAA838, hover #E69C2B, slot glow #FFAE00 at 50 percent on the recommended option; production green #2BE327, heat red #DA4535, red text #FF8E8E, blue #80CEF0 for links; shadow black at 35 percent; button minimum 108 by 28 with padding 0 8 0 8; container padding and spacing 4; slot size 40. Font Titillium Web (OFL 1.1) with a mono face for figures. No Wube or BiusArt sprite ever ships.

The same page on the phone (iPhone 16 Pro Max first, 430 CSS px, safe areas with a little extra gutter, build-notes 2 and 3) is the same panels, lamps and type, only stacked; a reviewer holding the phone next to the desktop sees one product (build-note 6).

The owner's earlier lock (the page markup and theme are not changed without an approved sample) is honoured by the path: the look ships as theme.css and page.html on dev, is screenshotted on desktop and phone sizes, read by the architect, sent to the owner with flaws named, then confirmed on the uat card before the merge, then promoted (nodes/N-48/spec.xml#owner-confirm, the one rule for who gates a page change). The owner's approval is the sample.
look.check: Playwright asserts the computed colours of the frame, caption, recommended option, lamp states, receipt marks and STALE mark against the values above on both viewport widths; the suite fails on a drift. The screenshot record on the promotion is the owner-facing proof.

cut-over.step: Ship dark: the Go page service runs as a dev tier beside the live Node stable; the Playwright suite passes against it; the look ticket lands on dev; screenshots to the owner.

uat: N-48 brings a uat tier up on the PR; because the cut-over PR carries the look (page.html and theme.css), N-28 posts the confirm card with the screenshot record and the owner confirms on the uat page itself before it merges (the one rule: nodes/N-48/spec.xml#owner-confirm).

Migrate state (one time, while the old stable keeps serving): coq owner import-answers and import-messages from ~/.bearings/coq-stable (dry-run, then --yes; counts and cmp of an export are the proof); questions.json's open cards become card records with their ids preserved.

Swap, by the system and never by hand: the merge of the cut-over ticket is a promotion for stable (N-48), and for the sha that carries tools/bearings/bin/cutover.sh the promotion handler starts the one-shot unit coq-cutover@coq-stable.service (Type=oneshot, ExecStart=tools/bearings/bin/cutover.sh --page coq-stable, installed by install-units.sh) instead of the in-place backend swap. The script, in order and each step idempotent: (a) refuses to run unless the import of step 3 is recorded (cutover.imported 100) and the watcher unit for the tier is alive (N-27), exit 4 with cutover.refused 412; (b) installs the units; (c) starts coq-watcher@coq-stable and coq-front-door@coq-stable; (d) reads the legacy pid from ~/.bearings/coq-stable/session.json and the legacy wait lock, sends SIGTERM, waits 10 s, then SIGKILL, and writes the pids it stopped into the record; (e) starts coq-bearings@coq-stable on port 44900 with the same key copied into server.json; (f) probes /health until page.up, 15 s; (g) writes cutover.swapped 201 (legacy pids, new pid, port, assets_hash) and the ledger row for N-33 itself. Any step that fails is retried 3 times 5 s apart; after the third the script restores the legacy server from the same session.json (server.mjs --join), writes cutover.failed 500 with the step and error, and N-28 cards it to the owner. A second run after cutover.swapped exits 0 and writes nothing. The phone URL does not change. The only hand path is the owner's one-time break glass named in the runbook, which runs the same unit and is counted by N-51 as a hand line operation.

Retire: make ask, make wait, reply.mjs, wait.mjs, server.mjs, front-door.mjs and the idle shutdown on stable are removed by the retire ticket after one day of the new stable serving with zero page.down 500; the Makefile verbs become wrappers over systemctl and the CLI. The old state root goes through cleanup-tier --legacy.

permissions.runs-as: the owner user, no sudo, MemoryMax 256M, listens on 127.0.0.1 only
permissions.may: subscribe to its tier's frames; call Intake.Answer with source page or controls and Inbox.Message; write page.* and file.stored; read and write its own state directory; read the repository assets of its checkout
permissions.may-not: write a ruling, a card, a reply or any other tier's records; expose the key; listen on a non-loopback address (N-34 does the tailnet); call herdr
permissions.owner-only: rotate-key; cleanup-tier on stable; the stable promotion break glass tools/bearings/scripts/promote.sh --tier stable --sha <sha> (N-48 runbook step 3); the cut-over break glass systemctl --user start coq-cutover@coq-stable (one time, counted by N-51). A seat that types either is refused: the scripts check the caller against the owner's uid and the absence of COQ_SEAT in the environment, exit 4 with control.refused 412.
